about: Running history of career questions put to Riley (by resume reviews, recruiters, or agents) and Riley's answers. Answers are edited for spelling, grammar, and tone, never copied verbatim, and never extended beyond what Riley said. Unanswered questions stay with status "open" and answer null. The site does not import this file; the resume skills read it as evidence alongside the rest of data/**/*.json.

statusValues.partial: Answered in part; the follow-up is listed in notes or as its own open entry.

entries.question: Have you ever owned or tracked a project budget, for example the KRAKEN contract, the ICARUS-Lite cost target, or purchasing in your ERP/CRM?
entries.answer: Yes. I began tracking project budgets at Filament Innovations, and at Proteor I track every engineering project: I estimate its budget, track it through the project, build its bills of materials, and maintain the unit cost of each product. This work runs in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, an ERP comparable to SAP.
entries.notes: Riley's ERP experience is Business Central, not SAP. Do not list SAP as a skill on that basis.

entries.question: Have you written customer quotes or proposals, or scoped and estimated work?
entries.answer: Yes. At Filament Innovations I wrote customer proposals, scopes of work, and estimates. At Proteor I no longer work with customers directly, except when a serious issue goes beyond what customer support can resolve. I present at Proteor's monthly USA review, where I cover project status, constraints, and budgets with Proteor leadership from its locations around the world; the meeting focuses on the U.S. departments.
entries.notes: Which Filament Innovations role(s) the proposal work belongs to is not yet recorded (see 2026-10-20-08).

entries.question: How large was the Business Central implementation (item count, timeline), and did you run the data migration and go-live?
entries.answer: The implementation covered more than 2,000 items and over 150 products and took five weeks. We spent the first two weeks evaluating the software, then three weeks migrating everything into the live system and reconciling inventory counts on the production floor.

entries.question: Is there a revenue figure or share you can give for ICARUS-Lite?
entries.clarification: Resumes currently say ICARUS-Lite was carried through commercialization "contributing to increased revenue", and reviewers want a number behind that phrase. Any one of these would do: revenue from ICARUS-Lite in a year, its share of the division's revenue, units sold against goal, or growth over the previous year.
entries.answer: The ICARUS-Lite unit goals were 60 units for 2025 and 100 units for 2026.
entries.notes: These are goals, not results. Units actually delivered are asked in 2026-10-20-06 and 2026-10-20-07.

entries.question: What does the 20-30% material consumption reduction from ExtrusionStudio measure?
entries.answer: It refers to label material, not filament. We used to print a full 8.5 x 11 inch sheet of labels for spools and spool boxes, with each sheet dedicated to one material and lot. Labels are now printed on demand, which eliminates that waste.
entries.notes: Riley cleared the label figure for publication. Do not describe this as raw material or filament savings. How the 20-30% was measured is asked in 2026-11-06-05.

entries.question: How does ExtrusionStudio tie its readings and alarms to the spool?
entries.answer: The program accounts for an offset, so its data and alarms align with what is landing on the spool. Alerts used to fire at the laser, while the error still had to pass through the accumulator before reaching the spool. We have since learned that this delay is one to two minutes.

entries.question: When did ExtrusionStudio go live, and on how many lines?
entries.answer: It went live around October 6-7, 2026 on all three lines. The thermal label printer was added on October 12, 2026.
entries.notes: Riley chose to keep the spool count private, so it is deliberately not recorded in this public repository.

entries.question: What does the upcoming ExtrusionStudio hardware update change?
entries.answer: It moves the system from a mini PC to a rack server with ECC memory and RAID 5 storage.
entries.notes: Planned, not yet shipped, so it stays off the site until it is running. The reason for the move and the backup plan are asked in 2026-11-06-06.

entries.question: How was the 20-30% label material reduction measured, given that the printer has been running only since October 12, 2026? Does it mean label stock used per spool, and how does it fit with print-on-demand leaving no waste?
entries.answer: It is based on the extra labels printed before the thermal printer was in place. Each sheet holds 18 labels, and a run rarely used a whole number of sheets, so the unused labels were wasted. A typical example works out to about 25% of the labels printed for that run.
entries.notes: This is an estimate from sheet arithmetic, not a measured before-and-after comparison, and the waste varies with run length. Run lengths are kept out of this public file.

entries.question: Why is ExtrusionStudio moving to the rack server, and how are spool records backed up beyond RAID?
entries.answer: The move is for data retention and to finish deploying cloud data.
entries.notes: The backup plan beyond RAID is not yet recorded. Stays off the site until the server is running.

entries.question: What decisions have you made from the extrusion data?
entries.answer: We do not yet have enough data to estimate lead times on large orders, but we can now estimate how many spools per material can be completed in a week, and we keep a running history of the schedule and material parameters. Running speed also correlates with temperature and humidity from day to day; more humidity makes the lines run slower.
entries.notes: Not on the site: ExtrusionStudio has been live only since October 2026, so the humidity effect is early data.

entries.question: What is an example of your role as the technical subject-matter expert?
entries.answer: In the plant, I bring industrial electronics experience to the extrusion lines and low-voltage sensor knowledge to the rest of the building. With customers, I am the go-to person for a quick and correct answer when troubleshooting product issues, whether mechanical, electrical, or most commonly user error, including how to mitigate the error, move forward, and learn from it.

entries.question: What is your role with your homeowners association?
entries.answer: I have been Treasurer since April 2026 for an association of about 80 units. I manage its banking and, as of November 2026, pay its monthly insurance. We are gradually establishing a community-focused board and moving away from a property management company. We recently went through a mid-year restructure, and I remain Treasurer.
entries.notes: Riley first said May, then gave April 2026 as the start date; April is used. Riley wants this on resumes. On 2026-11-07 Riley named the association, Carver House Homeowners Association, and asked for that name on the site and resumes; it replaces the earlier rule that the name stays off the site.

I also regularly work past the standard 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. day, remotely from home or at the shop after everyone else has gone home, where the quiet helps me finish the work I want done before the end of the day.

entries.question: Describe a specific production incident: what failed, how you found out, how long until service was restored, and what you changed afterward.
entries.answer: Nothing has failed in production. While moving ExtrusionStudio into production, I found and fixed two problems on the packing bench panel, the main panel where technicians approve or reject spools, add maintenance and production notes, and print labels: the screen lagged, and its connection was unreliable. I reduced the panel's animations from 60 to 30 frames per second, with no change in performance; checked whether the Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) was thermally throttling; and swapped in a temporary Pi with a new SD card and a fresh setup, with no difference. Running an Ethernet cable directly to the Pi fixed the screen's connectivity and the delay to the label printer, but not the lag. Moving the 1440p touch screen from 120% scaling to 1080p at 100% scaling removed the lag. I had tried 1440p at 100% scaling with no change, but that was before the Ethernet fix.
entries.notes: Riley plans to retest 1440p at 100% scaling on Monday, 2026-11-09, to see whether the lag was a connectivity issue all along; update this answer and the ExtrusionStudio design decision with the result. It is a go-live troubleshooting story, not an incident: never call it an outage. Added to the ExtrusionStudio project (designDecisions) on 2026-11-07.
